chains.title: G strengthens an activating TFAP2A–IRF6 enhancer connection

links.claim: TFAP2A is the favored AP-2-family factor for this site based on reported rs642961-specific allele-sensitive binding; the alt G allele is expected to bind more strongly than ref A. No QBiC-SELEX result or case-specific occupancy result is provided here.
The variant lies in a cis-regulatory element that can act as an IRF6 enhancer.
Greater TFAP2A binding increases enhancer output and IRF6 expression.
This enhancer effect occurs in developing craniofacial epithelium.
Increased IRF6 expression from the G allele lowers cleft-lip risk relative to the A allele.

predictions: In a relevant craniofacial epithelial context, the G allele shows greater TFAP2A binding than the A allele.
An otherwise matched enhancer assay shows greater activity from the G allele, accompanied by increased IRF6 expression.
falsified_if: Allele-matched assays in a relevant context show no greater TFAP2A binding or enhancer activity for G than A.
The G allele consistently lowers IRF6 expression in the relevant cell context.

chains.title: No TF-mediated effect of rs642961
predictions: In an appropriate cellular context, changing A to G at rs642961 produces no reproducible TF-mediated change in enhancer activity or IRF6 expression.
Any association with cleft lip could reflect linkage to another causal variant or another non-TF mechanism.
falsified_if: Precise allele editing or matched allele assays reproducibly show a TF-dependent change at rs642961 that alters IRF6 expression.

chains.title: G strengthens TFAP2A binding but reduces IRF6 enhancer output

links.claim: TFAP2A is the favored AP-2-family factor for this site based on reported rs642961-specific allele-sensitive binding; the alt G allele is expected to bind more strongly than ref A. No QBiC-SELEX result or case-specific occupancy result is provided here.
The variant lies in a cis-regulatory element that can act as an IRF6 enhancer.
In this alternative model, greater TFAP2A binding reduces enhancer output and IRF6 expression.
This repressive effect occurs in developing craniofacial epithelium.
Reduced IRF6 expression from the G allele increases cleft-lip risk relative to the A allele.

predictions: The G allele shows greater TFAP2A binding than the A allele.
An otherwise matched enhancer assay shows lower activity from the G allele, accompanied by reduced IRF6 expression.
falsified_if: The G allele increases enhancer activity and IRF6 expression in a relevant cell context.
Allele-matched assays show no greater TFAP2A binding for G than A.

matrix.test: Paired A-versus-G IRF6 enhancer reporter assay in a relevant craniofacial epithelial cell model, with IRF6 expression measured if feasible

outcomes.outcome: G produces greater enhancer activity than A, consistent with increased IRF6 expression.
G produces lower enhancer activity than A, consistent with reduced IRF6 expression.
No reproducible allele-dependent difference in enhancer activity or IRF6 expression.

next_experiment: Run a paired A-versus-G IRF6 enhancer reporter assay in a relevant craniofacial epithelial cell model; the direction of the activity difference distinguishes the two leading functional models.
